summary: ```# Introduction to New Features in Marvelous Designer 11 ## User Interface Changes Hello, everyone. Through this video, you will learn about the new features in Marvelous Designer 11. ### Main Page Navigation First, let's take a look at the changes in the user interface. In Marvelous Designer 11, you can switch the main page between **General** or **Store** through the label bar. You can see these two labels on the far left. - The **General** page is used to create clothes. - By selecting the **Store** label, you can view the products sold on the Marvelous Designer website. Now you can buy clothes directly in the software without visiting the website via the browser. ### Work Area Windows Using the previous version of Marvelous Designer, you could only open two work area windows at the same time. In the new version, you can select the window display by clicking on the lower right corner of the window. You can now display four work area windows simultaneously. - By clicking the **Remake** button, you can return to the default settings. - You can choose a suitable mode based on your usage by clicking the drop-down menu at the top of the work area window. ### Window Management At the top right corner of each window, you can find the **Copy** button. These pop-up windows can be dragged to the two windows on the screen and placed at will. - The two windows can be closed, hidden, or assembled with other windows. - Click the arrow button in the upper left corner to hide the window. When the window is hidden, it will appear in the form of a label bar on both sides. If you click the label, the window will appear again. - Click the **X** button in the upper right corner of the window to close it. Any pop-up window can be dragged to the existing window to merge them. Their names will appear in the form of a label at the bottom of the window. By clicking the label, you can view each window in the group. You can switch modes by clicking the drop-down menu at the top of the window. ### Multiple Modes and Linking Windows The user can use multiple modes in multiple windows at the same time. If you open multiple 3D windows simultaneously, you can use different tools in each window. The window on the 2D version will be linked to the 3D window you choose, so the tool you use will be displayed in the 2D window. - For example, if you click on a **fake needle tool** in a 3D window, you can see the corresponding changes in the 2D version. - You can edit or create a fake needle in the 2D window because they are linked. Similarly, if you choose the **move tool** in the 3D window, the 2D window will also switch to the selected version tool. However, you can only open one 2D window at the same time. This means that if you change a window to a 2D window through the drop-down menu, the original 2D window will be replaced. ### Managing Windows Once you choose a new window layout, you can select the 3D window you want to create. Click on **Managing** to organize your windows. You can also add a stamp to the number of windows left. The window layout can be reviewed by just clicking on the icon on the screen. - Click on **Managing** for the remaining windows. You can browse through it on the main page. - You can also select more than one window type as a unit of the window. ### Tool Integration In Marvelous Designer 11, more tools are integrated into the tool group. To make it easier to use, click on the **cutout line** on the pull-down menu or press the **Enter** key, and you can open the tool group in a spring form. - Any main menu with a cutout line can also be opened in spring form. - By clicking and dragging on the toolbar on the far left, you can open the tool group in a spring form. From the tool group, you can choose the position of the toolbar. You can hold the tool on one side of the toolbar and control the others on the opposite side. You can choose to display or hide the toolbar. ### Animation Editor Finally, click on the arrow at the bottom of the interface. You can open or close the **animation editor** and choose to display or hide the toolbar. ```
